A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 15-page Doc2Chart paper, including its appendices. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its hyperlink differ.

before.justification: v1 reports original chart-generation experiments across four LLMs in Table 3, human evaluations in Table 4, and evaluation-metric correlations with human judgments.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original chart-generation experiments, human evaluations, and metric-validation results in Sections 5–6 and Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Section 4 and the appendix prompts retain identical intent decomposition, iterative extraction, validation/refinement, heuristic-guided chart selection, and code generation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,242 intent-document-chart tuples from SEC financial filings and scientific papers sourced through SciDuet. No domains, tasks, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Single-step, Embedding retrieval, LLM retrieval, and LLM retrieval with query decomposition. Table 4 retains the same two human-evaluation baselines, and the metric-validation comparator is unchanged.

E3.justification: The four evaluated LLMs, document truncation to ±5 pages around supporting content, evaluation metrics, and human evaluation with 300 instances and three annotators remain identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the same metric validation against human judgments and the oil-price chart case study in Appendix A.1, Figures 4–6. No ablations, robustness tests, or sensitivity analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Human-rating aggregation, annotator/sample counts, and Pearson-correlation reporting are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and findings match, including Tables 3–4 and the appendix charts. For example, GPT-4o Doc2Chart data accuracy remains 75.18%, versus 67.38% for Single-step.

T1.justification: The task formulation, structured chart representation, and attribution reasoning in Sections 3 and 5.2 are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about the intent-driven task, training-free framework, attribution metric, curated dataset, and advantages over baselines.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and limitations remain identical, including chart-type subjectivity, lack of interactive clarification, context-window constraints, and possible contextual ambiguity in reference-free attribution.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, parsing tools, model identifiers, and appendix prompt templates in Figures 7–10 are unchanged. Technical and resource links match; only the arXiv stamp links to the newer paper version.

R1.justification: Section 2, the dataset comparisons in Table 2, and the bibliography are identical. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to prior research change.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 20 July 2025 to v2 dated 27 August 2025, with its hyperlink updated accordingly. Manuscript wording and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–15 render identically; page 1 differs only in the marginal version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The later PDF preserves all scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendix material. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its hyperlink produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
